title: Module 6 intro — Knowledge Integration and Data Handling

lines: Welcome to Module Six: Knowledge Integration and Data Handling.
When an agent answers wrong, the culprit is usually retrieval, not the model.
Picture a hospital assistant answering staff questions about internal policy.
It indexes twenty thousand documents, and the pilot looks great.
Then a nurse asks about a dosing policy and gets last year's version.
It was deleted at the source, but its chunks stayed in the index.
Another answer sits in a PDF table.
The parser flattened it into loose numbers, so no value matched its header.
Searches for exact form codes, like F-417, return loosely related pages.
Meaning-based search is weak on rare, exact strings like that.

say.0: Searches for exact form codes, like F four-seventeen, return loosely related pages.

lines: Worst, a nurse sees a salary review meant only for managers.
Nobody attached access rules to the chunks.
The first instinct is to buy a bigger model.
But every failure happened before the model saw a single word.
So the team rebuilds the pipeline, starting with extraction that keeps tables intact.
Chunks follow the headings and carry their source, date, and access level.
Hybrid search pairs vector search for meaning with keyword search for exact codes.
Then a reranker keeps only the best handful.
Deleted policies now leave the index immediately.
And searches are filtered by permission before anything is ranked.
The assistant cites the current policy, or admits its sources don't cover it.
And staff see only what they're allowed to.
Lesson one walks the production RAG pipeline, from extraction to generation.
You'll learn which stage causes which symptom.

say.0: Lesson one walks the production rag pipeline, from extraction to generation.

lines: Lesson two adds agentic retrieval: rewrite the query, grade the results, and retry a few times.
Knowledge graphs answer questions that join facts across documents.
Lesson three keeps the index fresh, correct, and permission-aware over time.
It also covers conflicting versions and personal data.
This domain is ten percent of the exam, and it loves symptom questions.
Wrong table numbers mean extraction; missed part numbers mean hybrid search.
Remember: a reranker reorders results, but can't find what retrieval missed.
Lesson one starts there: the pipeline, stage by stage.
